From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed bakeoff tests

Hi Caitlin — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and a proposed, lightweight bakeoff plan so your committee can evaluate objectively.

Pain points you emphasized:
- Long tail latency spikes on current vendor during peak EHR loads (P50/P95 variability).
- High per-token cost once you scale to batch clinical summarization jobs.
- Data residency and PHI handling: you need clear audit logs and optional VPC/on-prem runbook.

Primary goals for a winning vendor:
1) Predictable latency at scale (p95 < 350ms for interactive flows; consistent throughput for bulk summarization).
2) Cost predictability (clear cost per 1k tokens with batching savings).
3) Security/compliance proof points (SOC 2 Type II + HIPAA support or private deployment option).
4) Low integration friction (SDKs + prefix caching).

Decision criteria (what your committee will score): latency stability, average cost / 1k tokens, fidelity on clinical summaries (clinician-rated), deployment model options, and vendor support/SLAs.

Proposed 7-day bakeoff (suggested, flexible):
- Tests: 1) Interactive clinical Q&A (1000 synthetic sessions), 2) Bulk summarization (10k documents), 3) Rerank/embeddings spot-check.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, clinician ROUGE-like quality sample, error/ hallucination rate on a labeled 200-doc set.
- Baselines: Redwood default config vs CloudServe (your incumbent).
- Deliverables: runbook, raw metrics CSV, short executive slide with head-to-head scoring.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the bakeoff scope (above) and the test window you prefer.
2) Share your procurement timeline and any mandatory security attestations (SOC2/HIPAA specifics).
3) Give Rafael (SE) temporary access to the Vertex test environment or provide a sample dataset in our shared Drive.

I attached a short criteria sheet and the recording. Rafael and Neha are copied on this thread to coordinate the technical plan and commercial terms. If this looks good, can we lock dates for a 7-day run starting as early as Oct 19?

Thanks — looking forward to the committee run.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Folks — draft plan below. I kept it practical so we can spin up the runs quickly. If we get the test sandbox from Vertex by Tue EOD we can start data prep Wed and run Oct 19–25.

Bakeoff goals
- Repeatable head-to-head on the three workloads: interactive clinical Q&A, bulk summarization, embeddings/rerank.

Test harness (high level)
1) Environment: Redwood hosted + Dedicated variant; baseline: CloudServe endpoints (we'll call their public API). For security, run everything on masked data; if Vertex requests VPC testing, we will provide instructions and a temporary VPC config.
2) Models & configs: Redwood-standard small LLM (v1.3-quant), Redwood-larger (v2.0), CloudServe-default. For fairness, fix tokenizer settings and prompt templates.
3) Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency, request throughput, cost-per-1k-tokens (post-batching), clinician quality score (blind eval on 200 samples), hallucination count on labeled set, integration effort estimate (time to deploy).
4) Run cadence: 72-hour long continuous job for bulk summarization (simulate EHR ingest), 24-hour interactive session replay for latency profile (randomized concurrency up to 200 concurrent sessions).
5) Artifacts delivered: raw metrics CSVs, aggregated scoring sheet, short slide deck with recommended winner and rationale.

Technical needs from Vertex:
- Access to masked test dataset or S3 link (preferred) OR a sample set in our shared Drive.
- Allowlist for Redwood SE IPs if they want a VPC-only test.
- A contact for rapid triage if we see unexpected errors during the run.

Estimated Redwood resource use
- 1x senior SE (Rafael) for 2 calendar weeks (prep + run + analysis)
- 1x AE (Soojin/Neha) for comms and procurement
- GPU usage: approximate 4 A100-days for the largest tests (we can tighten if they prefer cheaper configs).

Questions for Neha: what is our recommended commercial credit to cover 7-day run for an org of this size? I suggest a modest credit (~$8k) to offset the cost and speed evaluation.

I'll produce a runnable checklist and a small script so we can reproduce locally.
